conclusion.justification: The report concludes that honey likely helps relieve acute cough symptoms in children over 1 year old based on moderate-to-low certainty evidence, presenting a cautiously favorable view.
conclusion.label: leans_endorse

report:
**Yes — honey likely helps relieve acute cough symptoms in children over 1 year old, though the evidence base has some limitations.**

Multiple systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials support this. A 2023 systematic review published in the *European Journal of Pediatrics* concluded that "honey seems to be more effective than a placebo/no treatment or cough medications in relieving symptoms of acute cough in children," though it rated the evidence quality as low-to-very-low (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00431-023-05066-1; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/).

The Cochrane systematic review, one of the most rigorous sources, found moderate-certainty evidence that honey reduces cough frequency better than no treatment or placebo, and moderate-certainty evidence that cough resolved sooner in children given honey versus salbutamol (mean difference −0.54 days) (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children; https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full). This is a meaningful update from Cochrane's earlier 2018 stance, which found no strong evidence either way.

Supporting clinical evidence includes a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in *Pediatrics* (300 children) finding that a single nocturnal dose of honey improved nocturnal cough and sleep quality compared to placebo.

The American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP) summarizes: for children 1–18 years old, honey "can reduce the frequency and severity of cough, as well as improve sleep for patients and parents, when compared with placebo or no treatment" (https://www.aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2016/0701/p20.html).

**Important caveat:** Honey must never be given to infants under 12 months due to botulism risk (Clostridium botulinum spores), per CDC/AAP guidance (https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/honey-botulism.html).

**Conclusion:** Yes, honey appears to help ease acute cough symptoms in children over age 1, supported by moderate-to-low certainty evidence, though larger high-quality trials are still needed.
